message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the family **Felidae** in the order **Carnivora**, while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the family **Equidae** in the order **Perissodactyla**.  
The most recent common ancestor of those two species is therefore the last common ancestor of the two orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla.  

That ancestor is a small, early placental mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous/early Paleocene, when the super‑order **Laurasiatheria** was beginning to diversify. In other words, the common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatherian mammals, a lineage that gave rise to many modern groups including carnivores, odd‑toed ungulates, even‑toed ungulates, bats, and whales.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) would be a common ancestor in the mammalian lineage. Both are mammals, but lions are felids (family Felidae), zebras are equids (family Equidae). They diverged from a common ancestor in the order Carnivora vs Perissodactyla? Actually lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla (odd-toed ungulates). So their common ancestor would be a more distant mammalian ancestor, perhaps the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: that would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of the superorders Laurasiatheria? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of lions and zebras would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria, which is a group of placental mammals that includes Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, and others. That ancestor would be a small mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. But maybe the question expects "the common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is a small mammal that lived about 70 million years ago." Or "the common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the superorder Laurasiatheria." Or "the common ancestor is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals." But the more precise answer: "The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria, which lived around 70-80 million years ago." Or "the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla." So answer accordingly.
